To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
prenatal exposure to psychopathology induces neuronal and immunological abnormalities in offspring and that these alterations precede behavioral changes.

Prenatal exposure of the fetus to maternal psychopathology induces molecular and cellular changes in umbilical cord cells and in the developing fetal brain, that are linked to impaired neurodevelopmental outcomes.
maternal psychopathology during pregnancy alters gene expression in the neonatal immune system, which is associated with impaired developmental outcomes in offspring.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that link maternal psychological distress to impaired offspring development, and how this process is shaped by maternal and offspring genotype.
the effects of prenatal stress exposure on the neurodevelopment and behavior of children.
the identification and characterization of molecular mechanisms through which prenatal exposure to maternal stress induces adverse behavioral and neurobiological outcomes in offspring.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
maternal psychopathology is a risk factor for neurodevelopmental outcomes and that the molecular mechanisms underlying this association are likely to be mediated via gene expression in cord blood.
maternal psychopathology induces neuronal, immunologic and behavioral abnormalities in offspring and supports the search for early biological markers of exposure to adverse in uterine environments.
maternal stress and depression are risk factors for adverse behavioral and developmental outcomes in offspring.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

maternal psychopathology, particularly depression, is associated with perturbed neurodevelopmental processes in the fetus and that these perturbations are evident at birth and may contribute to adverse outcomes in early childhood.
prenatal exposure to psychological distress induces molecular alterations in cord blood that are associated with adverse neurobehavioral outcomes in early life.
maternal psychopathology is associated with gene expression changes in cord blood that are enriched for genes implicated in brain function and neurodevelopmental disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
maternal psychopathology during the prenatal period can have a lasting impact on the health and development of their children.

the molecular alterations we identified in umbilical cord tissue of infants born to mothers with PTSD or depression are associated with the development of behavioral and cognitive abnormalities in the children at twenty-four months of age, and that this may be due to the impact of the maternal psychopathology on the developing brain of the fetus.

maternal psychopathology is linked to gene expression changes in cord blood and to impaired neurodevelopmental outcomes, which suggests that early biomarkers may be identified for children born to mothers with psychopathology.
